steps.text: Beat together egg, milk, cinnamon, vanilla and salt.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Soak bread slices in egg mixture for 20 second on each side, or until thoroughly coated. Cook bread until both sides are lightly browned and crisp. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy French Toast
raw_recipe.description: An easy to make crispy cinnamon French toast that will light up your morning.
raw_recipe.name: Easy French Toast

recipeInstructions.text: Beat together egg, milk, cinnamon, vanilla and salt.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Soak bread slices in egg mixture for 20 second on each side, or until thoroughly coated. Cook bread until both sides are lightly browned and crisp. Serve hot.

review.reviewBody: This recipe can be tinkered with-use 2 eggs to 1/8 c. of milk and cut back on the cinnamon to about 1/2 tsp. One way to mix the cinnamon in thoroughly is to mix all ingredients together EXCEPT the milk-add it last.

To get the best results, I found that you have to use 2 eggs, 1/2 tsp. of cinnamon, 1 tsp. vanilla, and a pinch of salt. You must also remember to keep stirring as you put each ingredient in, and ADD THE MILK LAST! In addition, 20 seconds is a little too long to soak each piece of bread. I would recommend around 10. This revised recipe turned out perfectly, and it tasted great! My brother said it was some of the best french toast he has ever tasted :) It only took about 15 minutes, like it said it would. I would definitely make it again, only NOT how the original 2-serving recipe said!

Too much milk to egg ratio! When I make French toast I use 4 eggs to about a 1/2 cream or half and half. A teaspoon of vanilla and a 1/2 to 1 teaspoon of cinnamon. Use a good heavy bread like French, Italian, Challah or croissants. Dip bread in mixture about 10-15 seconds, then I press it against the bowl to press out some of the liquid. Fry it in a skillet with canola oil or oil and butter mixture.

Mine gets nice and crisp without putting it in the oven.

If you only have white sandwich bread, cut it into 3 strips, and then dip it quickly, and put in hot pan. Otherwise you will have a sloppy mess. Cook them til they start to puff up and then turn. You need more oil to cook them than other breads.

I have been using this basic recipe for years. I only use 1/4cu of milk and a1/2tsp of cinnamon and white sugar mix. Cook on stove top for 3-4 minutes on first side and 2minutes on second size. I also melt a little butter in the pan before cooking. Oooooh soooo good
I found that for 2 servings, only half of each ingredient called for was needed, except for the egg. I also cooked each piece for around 35 seconds on medium heat. After adjustments, it was tasty!

I actually laughed when I read the quantity of each ingredient. I was even surprised that sugar was not an ingredient. Because I was making a lot anyway, I just used the same milk amount and did 5 eggs instead of 1. I also decreased the cinnamon to 1 tsp. You really need to use a mixer to get the cinnamon blended well. I added 1 tbsp of organic sugar, and I omitted the salt. I also like to dip mine in a little flour to get them crispy in the skillet! Sprinkle with a little powdered sugar, and YUM! I am surprised this recipe is even posted on this site. I have never had a bad recipe yet. Reading the reviews is what I always do first. It allows me to "play" with the recipe.

I just made this using sugggestions from the other reviewers. My 2 year old ate 2 slices and five year old, who is a little of a picky eater, ate one and asked to have it for lunch. I used 2 eggs, 1/8 cup milk, and only 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon. I didn't soak the bread for 20 seconds, just enough to coat both sides and it didn't seem soggy.

I fixed this for my husband and son. They loved it. The recipe I used said it was for 2 servings but I got more out of it then that. The bread I used I couldn't let soak or it got too dark while I was cooking it, so I just dipped it. A thicker bread would need soaked but what I had was thin.
Too much milk and cinnamon. Will try again with 1/4 cup milk and half teaspoon cinnamon.

This recipe could definitely use some improvements... 1/2 cup milk 2 teaspoon Pure Vanilla Extract 1 teaspoon Cinnamon, Ground 8 slices Cinnamon Swirl bread 2 egg 1. Beat egg, vanilla and cinnamon in shallow dish. Stir in milk. 2. Dip bread in egg mixture, turning to coat both sides evenly. 3. Cook bread slices on lightly greased nonstick griddle or skillet on medium heat until browned on both sides.

The flavors were good but they were just so soggy in the middle and nearly burnt on top. They may have been better baked in the oven, but who wants to do that? Or not soaked so long or not sure what…might try them again with 2 eggs, half of the milk, cinnamon and vanilla.

Way too much milk and after 20 seconds on each side the bread is so soaked that it falls apart into a soggy mess. There is so much milk and egg in the bread that after 10 mins at medium heat it got "brown" but not crispy. Smelled good because of the cinnamon but won't ever know how it tastes because the bread pretty much disintegrated into a soggy mess.
It came out soggy in the middle. I had to add more eggs to even out the ratio of the milk added. It was good though
Great French toast, easy to make with a lot of flavor!

I did this recipe as is and even with it looking burnt on the outside it was soggy evetime in the middle. I called my parents and they usually do 6 eggs and 1/4 cup of milk. This recipe had WAY too much milk for the small amount of eggs.
I made this recipe and definitely keeping it. It tastes so good and is really easy to make.

This smelled really good while it was cooking with the vanilla and cinnamon, but it was a fail all around. The ratio of milk to egg is way off. I cut this in half and used the full egg, half the milk, half the cinnamon, and half the vanilla. The batter made enough for 3 slices of bread after scaling it down to half, the bread was soggy and wet, and it needed a lot of sugar. I tried eating this without syrup, but it needs sugar to offset the spicy cinnamon. The middles of the bread was gummy and not pleasant even though the edges seemed set and browned. I tried two bites, but I didn't like this at all. I don't like custardy french toast and this just did not appeal to me. Too much milk, too much cinnamon, no sugar, soggy middles, too much tinkering required to make it palatable. I would not fix this again.
quick easy and can easily be scaled for more
I am flabbergasted by some of the low reviews. It was simple, quick and tasted great. For those complaining of soggy results, use a hotter skillet/griddle. Thank you!

Made an acct just to warn others to never, NEVER, use this recipe!!!! The only reason it got one star is cause thats the lowest allowed to leave a review. The amount of milk and cinnamon in this recipe are about 4 times the amount needed. Not to mention the time suggested to soak in the mix before cooking. The "toast" gets so soggy it becomes completely unmanageable while cooking and what you end up with is what I can only describe as a scrambled egg version of what this recipe said it would make.
